intro.data: From a form you can read a name and an age. The tray holds two pairing machines; bring the right one onto the board and wire the form to the record — so Get Name gives the name and Get Age gives the age. One pairing builds it right; the other swaps the fields. Leave the swapper in the tray.
intro.alchemy: From a seed you can draw salt and sulfur. The tray holds two pairing apparatus; bring the right one onto the board and wire the seed to the compound, correctly ordered. One is right; the other swaps. Leave the swapper in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: From a caster you can draw light and heat. The tray holds two pairing runes; bring the right one onto the board and wire the caster to the blend, correctly ordered. One is right; the other swaps. Leave the swapper in the tray.
intro.abstract: ⟨f,g⟩ runs both maps and pairs the results into (a,b), holding both a and b; π₁/π₂ then pull out the first/second. From the tray bring the pairing that sends x ↦ (3,4) and wire X to A×B; leave the swapped one (x ↦ (4,3)) in the tray.

goal.data: Bring the right pairing from the tray and wire the form to the record so Get Name→name and Get Age→age.
goal.alchemy: Bring the right pairing from the tray and wire the seed to the compound so the projections recover salt and sulfur.
goal.spellcraft: Bring the right pairing from the tray and wire the caster to the blend so the projections recover light and heat.
goal.abstract: Bring the correct ⟨f,g⟩ from the tray and wire X to A×B.

description.alchemy: a compound blending salt and sulfur
description.spellcraft: a blend of light and heat

description.data: packs the form into a record — name first, age second
description.alchemy: packs the seed into a compound — salt first, sulfur second

description.abstract: pairs the two outputs: sends x ↦ (3,4) (so π₁ recovers 3, π₂ recovers 4)
the swapped pairing: sends x ↦ (4,3) — components in the wrong order

afterSuccess.data: Your pairing built the record so each projection reads back the right field. The swapped pairing put age where the name should be. There is exactly one ⟨f,g⟩ that fits — that uniqueness defines the product.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Your pairing packed the compound so each projection reads the right component. The swap misordered it. Exactly one ⟨f,g⟩ fits — uniqueness defines the product.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Your pairing wove the blend so each projection reads the right essence. The swap misordered it. Exactly one ⟨f,g⟩ fits — uniqueness defines the product.
afterSuccess.abstract: The correct pairing makes π₁∘⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂∘⟨f,g⟩ = g; the swap does not.

reveal.summary: The universal property: for any f : X→A and g : X→B there is a UNIQUE ⟨f,g⟩ : X→A×B with π₁∘⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂∘⟨f,g⟩ = g.
reveal.moreFormal: This determines A×B up to isomorphism. A pairing that swaps components fails the projection laws.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: x => ({ name: f(x), age: g(x) }) — swapping the fields breaks the accessors.
